Q4501499.summary: Christ looks out directly at the viewer, bearded and long-haired, his head set against a large golden halo. He blesses with his right hand and holds in his left a heavy Gospel book whose cover is studded with jewels and a cross. Painted in hot wax, the face is subtly asymmetrical, which many have read as a meditation on Christ's two natures, divine and human. It is the earliest known surviving icon of Christ as Pantocrator, 'Ruler of All', and one of the most important works of Byzantine art.
facts: For a time the icon was thought to date from the 13th century, because it had been almost completely overpainted then; only in 1962 was it recognized as mid-6th-century work.
It survived Byzantine Iconoclasm because Sinai had already passed under Muslim rule, beyond the reach of the iconoclast emperors.
The panel, now 84 cm high, was originally taller and wider before its top and sides were cut down.
Q4501499.notes: Production in Constantinople is a widely held inference (possible imperial gift at the monastery's foundation, 548–565), not a documented fact.
